subject: Strength of Materials
summary: shear force and bending moment diagrams for cantilevers, simply supported and overhanging beams under point loads, UDLs, varying loads and couples
next_day: Strength of Materials, Bending & Shear Stresses

questions.text: The 3 m cantilever shown carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length and a 5 kN point load at the free end. The bending moment at the fixed end has magnitude
solution: Concept: For a cantilever, take moments of all loads on the free side of the section; no reactions are needed.
From the point load: 5 × 3 = 15 kN·m
From the UDL: (4 × 3) × 1.5 = 18 kN·m
M = 15 + 18 = 33 kN·m (hogging); the SF at the fixed end is 5 + 12 = 17 kN.
Exam tip: 51 kN·m results from placing the UDL resultant at the free end instead of at its centroid.

questions.text: The simply supported beam shown carries two 20 kN loads placed symmetrically. The maximum bending moment (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: By symmetry each reaction is half the total load.
R<sub>A</sub> = R<sub>B</sub> = 20 kN
Under each load: M = 20 × 1.5 = 30 kN·m
Between the loads the SF is zero, so the BM stays constant at 30 kN·m: this middle region is in pure bending, the set-up used in four-point bending tests.
Exam tip: Zero SF over a length means constant BM over that length.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span L carries a UDL w over the whole span. The shear force at a section L/4 from a support has magnitude
solution: Concept: V(x) = RA − wx with RA = wL/2.
The SFD is a straight line from +wL/2 to −wL/2, crossing zero at midspan.
Exam tip: The BM there is M = (wL/2)(L/4) − w(L/4)²/2 = 3wL²/32.

questions.text: The simply supported beam shown carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole 5 m span and a 40 kN point load at 2 m from A. The maximum bending moment (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: Find the reactions, then locate where the SF changes sign; the BM is maximum there.
SF just left of the point load: 49 − 10 × 2 = +29 kN; just right: 29 − 40 = −11 kN → sign change at x = 2 m
Exam tip: With a point load present, check whether the SF crosses zero inside a UDL segment or jumps through zero at the load. Here it jumps.

questions.text: A sudden vertical jump in the bending moment diagram of a beam occurs at the section where
solution: Concept: dM/dx = V. A point load makes V jump, so the BMD only changes slope there (a kink).
A concentrated couple M₀ adds M₀ to the moment over an infinitesimal length, so the BMD jumps by M₀ while the SFD is unaffected.
A UDL changes the slope of the SFD; a support reaction is just a point force.
Exam tip: SFD jumps ↔ point forces; BMD jumps ↔ point couples.

questions.text: The beam ABC shown has a span AB of 4 m and an overhang BC of 1 m. It carries 20 kN at the middle of AB and 10 kN at C. The distance of the point of contraflexure from A (in m) is ______
solution: Concept: Point of contraflexure: BM = 0 (with a sign change) away from a free end or simple support.
Moments about B: R<sub>A</sub> × 4 = 20 × 2 − 10 × 1 → R<sub>A</sub> = 7.5 kN; R<sub>B</sub> = 22.5 kN
M = 0 → x = 3.2 m; M is +15 kN·m under the 20 kN load and −10 kN·m at B.
Exam tip: Overhanging beams almost always have a point of contraflexure; sketch the BMD sign at each key point first.

questions.text: A 4 m cantilever carries a load varying linearly from zero at the free end to 6 kN/m at the fixed end. The bending moment at the fixed end has magnitude
solution: Concept: Replace the triangular load by its resultant at the centroid of the triangle.
Resultant = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 kN, acting at L/3 = 4/3 m from the fixed end
Exam tip: If the triangle were reversed (maximum at the free end), the lever arm would be 2L/3 and M = wL²/3 = 32 kN·m.

questions.text: The simply supported beam AB shown (span 8 m) carries only an anticlockwise couple of 40 kN·m at C, 3 m from A. The maximum magnitude of the bending moment (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: The reactions form a couple: R = M₀/L. Then the BMD is two parallel straight lines with a jump of M₀ at C.
R = 40/8 = 5 kN: R<sub>A</sub> = 5 kN upward, R<sub>B</sub> = 5 kN downward
Just left of C: M = 5 × 3 = +15 kN·m
An anticlockwise couple lowers the BM by 40: just right of C, M = 15 − 40 = −25 kN·m, then it rises linearly to 0 at B.
|M|max = 25 kN·m
Exam tip: The jump splits as M₀a/L and M₀b/L on either side: 40 × 3/8 = 15 and 40 × 5/8 = 25.

questions.text: The SFD of a simply supported beam of span 6 m is a single straight line falling from +30 kN at A to −30 kN at B. The maximum bending moment in the beam is
solution: Concept: dV/dx = −w and the area of the SFD gives the change in BM.
Slope = 60/6 = 10 kN/m → a UDL of 10 kN/m over the whole span
Mmax = area of the positive SFD triangle = ½ × 3 × 30 = 45 kN·m (= wL²/8 ✔)
Exam tip: Reading loads from an SFD: slope = load intensity, jumps = point loads.

questions.text: A 3 m cantilever carries a UDL of 10 kN/m only over the 2 m length next to its free end (the 1 m next to the support is unloaded). The magnitude of the bending moment at the fixed end (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: Resultant of a partial UDL acts at the middle of the loaded length.
Resultant = 10 × 2 = 20 kN, at 1 m from the free end, i.e. 2 m from the support
Over the unloaded 1 m the SF is constant (20 kN) and the BM varies linearly.
Exam tip: If the same UDL were next to the support instead, M would be only 20 × 1 = 20 kN·m.

questions.text: A beam of length L rests on two supports placed symmetrically at a distance a from each end and carries a UDL over its whole length. For the least value of the maximum bending moment (hogging at the supports = sagging at mid-span), a should be about
solution: Concept: Equate the hogging moment over a support to the sagging moment at mid-span.
Hogging: wa²/2. Sagging at centre: (wL/2)(L/2 − a) − wL²/8 = wL²/8 − wLa/2
wa²/2 = wL²/8 − wLa/2 → 4a² + 4aL − L² = 0
Exam tip: A classic GATE result; the supports are then 0.586L apart.

questions.text: The simply supported beam shown (span 6 m) carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its right half. The maximum bending moment (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: The maximum BM is where the SF is zero, which lies inside the loaded half.
R<sub>A</sub> = 60 × 1.5/6 = 15 kN; R<sub>B</sub> = 45 kN
Exam tip: The maximum is NOT at mid-span (M there is 45 kN·m) and not under the centre of the load.

questions.text: On a portion of a beam between two point loads, with no other load on that portion, the bending moment diagram is
solution: Concept: w = 0 → V is constant → dM/dx is constant.
So the BMD is a straight line (horizontal if V = 0 there, as in Q2).
A parabola needs a UDL; a cubic needs a linearly varying load.
Exam tip: Degree rule: load degree n → SF degree n + 1 → BM degree n + 2 (point loads count as 'no distributed load').

questions.text: A 2 m cantilever carries a 10 kN load at its free end inclined at 30° to the axis of the beam, as shown. The magnitude of the bending moment at the fixed end (in kN·m) is ______
solution: Concept: Only the component of the load perpendicular to the beam axis bends the beam; the axial component causes direct (axial) force.
Transverse component = 10 sin 30° = 5 kN; axial component = 10 cos 30° = 8.66 kN
Exam tip: 17.32 kN·m (using cos 30°) is the trap: check which angle is given, with the axis or with the vertical.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span L carries two equal point loads W at L/3 and 2L/3 from one support. The maximum bending moment is
solution: Concept: Symmetric loading: each reaction = W.
Under each load: M = W × L/3 = WL/3; between the loads the SF is zero and the BM stays at WL/3.
Compare: a single central load 2W would give 2W × L/4 = WL/2.
Exam tip: For loads at distance a from each support, Mmax = Wa over the whole middle region.
